info.title: Propel MBOM API
info.summary: Create, read, edit, baseline and reconcile a Manufacturing BOM.
info.description:
The complete REST surface of Propel's Manufacturing BOM (MBOM), built on the new
**branch / baseline / configuration-item** framework. Eight endpoints cover the whole
lifecycle: create an MBOM over a released eBOM revision, read its structure, edit it with
delta operations, freeze it as a baseline, and reconcile it against a newer eBOM revision.

---

## Read this first: the eight ideas the whole API rests on

### 1. An MBOM inherits its structure. It never copies it.

Creating an MBOM writes **four records and not one row of BOM structure**. The branch stores
only its own *deltas*; everything else is resolved at read time by walking the live legacy
`Assembly__c` graph beneath the accepted eBOM root revision. An untouched branch holds zero
per-edge records however many times it is read.

### 2. `T_R` — the pinned source clock

When an MBOM is created (or a pull is committed), the accepted root revision's
**release date** is stamped once as `Source_TimePoint__c`. That timestamp is **T_R**, and every
inherited row resolves against it: a child item renders at whichever revision was released as
of T_R.

T_R is *stamped, then read* — never re-derived. So when engineering releases `Assy-100` rev-2,
**nothing happens to the MBOM**. It still resolves against rev-1's T_R until someone explicitly
accepts the newer revision with a [pull](#tag/Pull).

### 3. `asOf` — the branch clock, and why there are two

Every read also takes an `asOf` timestamp (defaulting to now). That one governs the *branch's*
own content — its deltas, its locally added parts, its substitutes.

Two clocks are therefore legitimately in play at once, and each row states which one governs it
(`TreeRowDTO.governingTimestamp`, `MemberState.governingClock`):

| Row kind | Governing clock |
|---|---|
| `inherited` — supplied by the source, untouched | **T_R** (`source`) |
| `claimed` — the branch took copy-on-write ownership | **T_R** for the child revision it pins |
| `local` — branch-owned, no upstream provenance | **`asOf`** (`branch`) |
| a *substitute* (from `replace`) | **`asOf`** — its child floats |

A direct consequence is that **one item can render at two different revisions in the same
tree**. That is expected, not a fault, and is reported as a `mixed-revision` warning beside the
data rather than an error instead of it.

### 4. Provenance: `inherited` / `claimed` / `local`

Derived at read time, never stored. `claimed` and `local` differ by exactly one field on the
winning delta row (`Overrides_Source__c` set vs. null), and that difference is what makes
"what did I change relative to upstream?" answerable.

### 5. Copy-on-write: you must `claim` before you can edit

An inherited row is read-only. Editing it is refused with `CLAIM_REQUIRED`, carrying the eBOM
line id so the client can offer the claim. Divergence from upstream is always an explicit act.

### 6. Nothing is ever deleted

Removal is an **exclude delta** — a tombstone appended to an append-only log. `restore` lifts
it. A hard delete of any branch-owned row is refused (`HARD_DELETE_BLOCKED`). This is what makes
a read at a past `asOf`, and therefore a baseline, reproducible.

### 7. A baseline stores a timepoint, not rows

Cutting a baseline records one timestamp and freezes the revisions it resolved to. Reading it
**re-resolves** the branch at that timestamp. Two stored counts act as canaries
(`BASELINE_COUNT_DRIFT`, `BASELINE_PROVENANCE_DRIFT`) if something the resolution depends on has
moved since.

### 8. "Pull", not "merge"

A pull is the **downstream-initiated acceptance of a newer upstream source version**, matching
`Branch_Source_CI__c.Source_Type__c`. The word *merge* is deliberately reserved for the Phase 2
branch-to-branch operation, which is bidirectional and common-ancestor-based — genuinely
different.

---

## Response and error conventions

The MBOM API does **not** use the Propel framework's `RestResponseHandler`. Each route
serialises through `MbomHttp` directly onto the HTTP response, so:

- Success and error bodies are **plain JSON, never wrapped** in the framework's
  `entity` / `entities` envelope.
- **Error bodies key the code as `code`, not `errorCode`.** `errorCode` is the framework's key;
  it appears in this API only *inside* a delta batch's per-operation `results[]`.
- **Nulls are not suppressed.** A field a producer never set for that case is genuinely absent
  or explicitly `null`, and the two are meaningful — see `DeltaResult.forked`.
- `code` values come from `MbomErrorCode`, a fixed enum. **The code is the contract; the message
  is not.** Messages are Custom Labels and are translated; switch on `code`, never on text.

### Status-code scheme

| Status | Meaning |
|---|---|
| **400** | The request could not be read, or a value is out of range. Fix the request. |
| **403** | No permission. The body carries the label only — never the object that was denied. |
| **404** | The path, or an id in the body, names nothing. |
| **409** | Well formed, and **retryable after changing state** — claim it first, restore it first, re-preview. |
| **413** | More than 200 operations in one delta batch. |
| **422** | Well formed, but **impossible against the model**. Retrying unchanged will never succeed (a cycle is still a cycle). |
| **500** | Unmodelled server failure. Carries the exception type and message, never the stack trace. |

The 409/422 split is deliberate: a client that retries on a generic 4xx would spin forever on a
cycle, and the two cases want different UI.

---

## Design intent: MBOM-specific paths, generic vocabulary

MBOM is the first application of a general branch / baseline / configuration-item framework. The
path is namespaced under `/mbom` so MBOM-only rules have somewhere to live, but the nouns below
that segment — **branch**, **source**, **member**, **override**, **baseline** — are framework
concepts, not MBOM concepts. Everything MBOM-specific is confined to a single discriminated
schema, `AssemblyEdgeDetail`, reached through `MemberState.detail` and keyed by `ciType`. A
second configuration-item type adds a sibling schema there and touches nothing else.

## Routing

Routed through `EntryAPI` → `EntryRoute` → `MbomRoute` → (`MbomCreateRoute` | `MbomBranchRoute` |
`MbomSourceRoute` | `MbomBaselineRoute`) in `src/main/default/classes/api/`, **not** a standalone
`@RestResource`.

Note there is **no `branchId` path segment on the source endpoints**: a source already names its
owning branch through `Branch_Source_CI__c.Downstream_Branch__c`. `branchId` still appears in the
pull-preview *body*, denormalised for display.

post.summary: Create an MBOM over a released eBOM revision
post.description:
Creates an MBOM header, its first branch, the branch's eBOM source lineage, and that
source's first acceptance — **four records in one transaction, and zero rows of BOM
structure** (`MbomCreateService`).

The response returns all four ids rather than just `mbomId`, because a caller that had to go
looking for the other three would be querying schema this API exists to hide. The one you
will use most is `branchSourceCiId` — it is the `sourceId` every `/sources/...` endpoint
takes.

## The root revision must be Released

Its `Released_Date_Time__c` becomes **T_R**, the timepoint every inherited row is pinned at.
An unreleased revision has no such date, so there is nothing to pin to.

Four shapes are refused with `NOT_RELEASED` (409, not 400 — releasing the revision makes the
identical request succeed): not released; **Cancelled**; **Expired**; released but carrying
no release date. Cancelled and Expired are excluded because the eBOM's own as-of read would
never resolve them either.

## Timestamps stamped here

| Field | Value | Why it matters |
|---|---|---|
| `Source_TimePoint__c` (**T_R**) | the root revision's release date | what inherited rows resolve at, forever |
| `Accepted_At__c` | the **wall clock**, now | which acceptance governs a given `asOf` |

A consequence worth knowing before you write a test: because `Accepted_At__c` is the wall
clock, a branch created now renders **nothing** when read at an `asOf` in the past. That is
the acceptance not existing yet at that timestamp, not a defect.

## Access

Gated **before the body is read**: a caller with no create grant gets 403 whatever they sent.
Requires create on `MBOM__c`, `Branch__c`, `Branch_Source_CI__c` and
`Branch_Source_CI_Rev__c`, plus read on `Item_Revision__c`. All five are named so a partial
grant is a clean 403 rather than a 500 out of the middle of the DML.

201.description:
Created. Four records now exist. 201 rather than 200 because the response names records
that did not exist before the call, and a client distinguishing "created" from "already
there" has nothing else to read.

400.description:
`INVALID_REQUEST` — the body was empty or unreadable; `mbomName` or `branchLabel` was
blank; or either exceeded its field length (`mbomName` ≤ 80, `branchLabel` ≤ 80 — the
shorter of `Branch__c.Name` at 80 and `Label__c` at 255).

A malformed id in the **body** is a 400 while one in the **URI** is a 404, and that is
not an inconsistency: the URI is what *names* the resource, so a path naming nothing is
a path to nothing. A body field is a value in a request to a resource that does exist.

value.message: That request could not be read. Check that the body is valid JSON and that every required value is supplied. (mbomName is required)

404.description:
`NOT_FOUND` — `rootItemRevisionId` was null, is not an `Item_Revision__c` id, or names
no visible row. The three are not distinguished on purpose: separating "malformed" from
"absent" would tell an unauthorised caller which ids exist.

value.message: That record does not exist, or you do not have access to it. (a0Bg8000000Ab10EAC is not an Item_Revision__c)

409.description:
`NOT_RELEASED` — the root revision is unreleased, Cancelled, Expired, or has no release
date, so there is no T_R to stamp.

value.message: An mBOM can only be created from a released item revision. (a0Ag8000000Ab99EAC)

get.description:
The branch's resolved content at one timepoint: the eBOM traversed at **T_R**, with the
branch's own deltas folded and overlaid at **`asOf`**.

This is the main read. It is where the two-clock model becomes visible — every row states
its own `provenance` and its own `governingTimestamp`, because a row that did not carry its
own clock would be unexplainable to the person looking at it.

## What the response contains that you might not expect

- **Excluded rows are rendered**, carrying `isExcluded: true`. A tree read shows the person
  editing what was removed. (A *baseline* read filters them out — see that endpoint.)
- **`isEditable: false`** on any row inside the subtree of a locally added or substituted
  assembly. Only content the branch's *source* supplied can be claimed or changed. It is
  stated rather than left to be derived from `provenance`, so a client does not have to
  encode which provenance values happen to be editable this release. Every delta op refuses
  these rows, so a UI offering an action on one is offering an action the API will reject.
- **Unreachable rows are dropped.** A delta can name a parent item that is not in the tree —
  a subassembly whose item had nothing released at T_R drops out, and a claim beneath it
  survives the overlay as a row with an absent parent. This read walks down from the root and
  keeps only what it can reach, in **both** shapes.
- **`warnings` and `rows` are always present**, empty rather than absent. A client that has
  to distinguish "no warnings" from "the key is missing" writes null checks at every call
  site, and one of them is eventually forgotten.

## Flat vs. nested, and a real trap

`flat=true` (the **default**) returns one row per edge, each carrying `parentItemId` and an
empty `childRows` — losslessly re-nestable by the client. `flat=false` nests via `childRows`.

**The nested shape duplicates a shared subassembly; the flat shape does not.** The traversal
walks a DAG and emits a shared subtree once; nesting re-materialises it under every parent
that uses it, because that is what a BOM tree looks like to a person expanding it. So the two
shapes carry the same *content* but not the same row **count** — never treat a nested row
count as a total — and a deeply shared DAG can hit heap nested while rendering comfortably
flat.

## Reads create nothing

No DML anywhere on this path. An untouched branch stays at zero rows however many times it
is read.

flat.summary: Flat (default) — inherited, claimed, local and excluded rows

400.description:
`ASOF_INVALID` — `asOf` could not be parsed. `ASOF_IN_FUTURE` — `asOf` is later than now;
there is no configuration at a timepoint that has not happened.

value.message: The timepoint could not be read. Use an ISO-8601 timestamp, for example 2026-02-01T00:00:00Z. (yesterday)

422.description:
`EBOM_CYCLE` — the source eBOM itself contains a cycle, so its structure cannot be
resolved. Fix the eBOM; retrying is pointless.

get.summary: Read what a source supplies, with no branch deltas applied
get.description:
The "**what would I inherit?**" read: the structure as one source supplies it, with the
branch's claims, excludes and replaces deliberately **not** overlaid.

Use it to answer "what did I change relative to upstream?" by diffing this against
`GET /mbom/branches/{branchId}/tree`. Every row comes back `provenance: inherited`.

## Why there is no `flat` parameter

A source's own structure has no deltas overlaid on it, so there is no nesting decision to
make. An unexpected `flat` is **ignored rather than rejected**, so one parameter set can be
sent to both tree reads.

400.description: `ASOF_INVALID` or `ASOF_IN_FUTURE` — see the branch tree read.

422.description: `EBOM_CYCLE` — the source eBOM contains a cycle.

post.summary: Apply a batch of delta operations to a branch
post.description:
The single write endpoint for editing a branch. Eight operations — `claim`, `update`, `add`,
`exclude`, `restore`, `replace`, `revert`, `convert-to-native` — arrive in one array and are
applied under one envelope.

**Returns `200`, not `201`**, even though rows are created: the response is a *report* on a
set of operations, not a pointer to one new resource, and under `atomic: false` some of them
may have failed.

## How a batch executes

1. **Size check** — more than 200 operations is `BATCH_TOO_LARGE` (413), refused before
   anything is resolved.
2. **One snapshot.** The branch is resolved **once**, at `asOf`. That is the whole reason a
   batch endpoint exists: twenty operations resolving the branch each would be twenty
   traversals, and the tree could shift underneath the batch halfway through.
3. **Validate everything, then apply.** Two passes, never interleaved, so *every* fault is
   reported rather than only the first.
4. **Persist** in a fixed number of DML statements — twenty claims cost the same statements
   as one.

### Order is preserved, but order is not sequencing

Results come back in request order with your `clientRef` echoed and `index` stated. But
**every operation validates against the one pre-batch snapshot, so a later operation cannot
see an earlier one's effect.** `[claim(L), update(L)]` in one batch answers `CLAIM_REQUIRED`
on the update — and under the default `atomic: true` that rejects the whole batch.

> **Dependent edits are two requests, not two operations.**

## `atomic` — the failure contract is yours to choose

| `atomic` | Behaviour |
|---|---|
| `true` (**default** — a null wins the safer contract) | All-or-nothing. Any validation failure throws: the status is the **first failure's** own code (so a batch whose only fault is `CLAIM_REQUIRED` still answers 409, not a generic 400) and the body carries a `failures[]` array with **every** failure. The branch is left exactly as it was. |
| `false` | Apply what is valid, report the rest. `200` with per-operation `results[]`. |

`atomic: false` reports per-operation **validation** failures only. It does not fall back to
per-operation DML: the aggregate is one savepoint and one set of statements, and a failure
there rolls the batch back and propagates.

## `asOf` chooses what a batch *validates* against; it never dates the write

Every row written is effective **now**, whatever `asOf` says. A past `asOf` means "validate
against the configuration as it stood then" — optimistic concurrency, not time travel.
Backdating the write would let a batch win the current fold *and* change what a read at an
intervening timestamp returned, rewriting history in an append-only log.

Several operations therefore **refuse a past `asOf` outright** with `INVALID_REQUEST`,
because they decide from the branch's *current* state: `restore`, `revert`,
`convert-to-native`, and any `claim` / `add` / `exclude` / `replace` that has to mint a new
edge identity.

## `Idempotency-Key`

Read and passed through, and **ignored this phase**. It is accepted so a client can start
sending it now without its first request failing, and a later phase can honour it without a
breaking change.

## The operations

| `op` | Required fields | What it does |
|---|---|---|
| `claim` | `ebomAssemblyId` | Takes one live eBOM line into the branch as a copy-on-write override, so the branch can diverge from it. Copies the values as they stand. Writes 5 records. |
| `update` | `assemblyCiId` **or** `ebomAssemblyId`; `quantity` and/or `findNumber` | Revises a branch-owned edge. Edits its `CI_Rev__c` in place while Draft; otherwise allocates a new revision, freezes the old one, and returns `forked: true`. Membership is not touched. |
| `add` | `parentItemId`, `childItemId`, `quantity`, `findNumber` | Adds a part the eBOM never supplied — packaging, fixtures, consumables. Branch-**local**: `Overrides_Source__c` stays null, and the child **floats** at `asOf`. |
| `exclude` | `ebomAssemblyId` **or** `ciId` | Tombstones a row. **No cascade is written** — the descendant prune is computed at read time, because a descendant still supplied through another path must survive. |
| `restore` | `ciId` | Lifts an exclusion. Appends `Add` when the branch holds content for the row, or `Revert` when it does not (an inherited row excluded straight from a stub) — appending `Add` blindly would break the next read. |
| `replace` | `replacedEbomAssemblyId`, `newChildItemId`, `quantity`, `findNumber` | Substitutes a different child for the one an eBOM line supplies, **recording that it is a substitution** (`Replaces__c`), so the pair does not read as an unrelated removal plus an unrelated addition. |
| `revert` | `ciId` **or** `ebomAssemblyId` | Discards the branch's override so the row falls back to what its source supplies. Nothing on disk is touched — a `Revert` marker is appended and the fold drops it entirely. |
| `convert-to-native` | `ciId` | Severs a claimed edge's link to the source it overrides: same content, but now branch-owned in its own right (`provenance` flips `claimed` → `local`). Appends an `Add` with `Overrides_Source__c` null. |

### Addressing quirks worth knowing

- `update` accepts `ebomAssemblyId` **and has to**: an inherited row has no edge record, so
  that is the only id a client holds for the row whose update must come back
  `CLAIM_REQUIRED`. Without it the rejection could never be reached.
- `revert` accepts `ebomAssemblyId` for the mirror reason: a reverted row renders with no
  `CI__c` at all, so a *second* revert — which must answer `NO_OVERRIDE` — cannot be
  addressed any other way.
- `replace` only works on eBOM-derived rows. A branch-**local** row has a synthetic
  `local-…` edge key and no `Assembly__c` line, so replacing local content is `update`, or
  `exclude` plus `add`.

## Access

Requires **create** on `Assembly_CI__c`, `CI__c`, `Assembly_CI_Rev__c`, `CI_Rev__c` and
`Branch_Member__c`, **and edit** on `Assembly_CI__c` (upserted) and `CI_Rev__c` (updated when
an operation freezes a predecessor). Create and edit are not the same permission, and both
are named so a partial grant is a 403 before any DML.

parameters.name: Idempotency-Key
parameters.description:
Accepted and **ignored** this phase. Present so a client can start sending it without
its first request failing.

claimThenEdit.summary: Claim two eBOM lines (atomic, the default)

update.summary: Revise quantity and find number on a claimed edge

addLocal.summary: Add a part the eBOM never supplied

excludeAndReplace.summary: Substitute an alternate part, and drop another line

nonAtomic.summary: Best-effort — apply what is valid, report the rest

200.description:
The batch report. Also returned when `atomic: false` and some operations failed — check
`failed` and each `results[].success`, not the status code.

forked.summary: An update that had to fork a frozen revision

400.description:
`INVALID_REQUEST` — the body could not be read; or (under `atomic: true`) an operation
failed validation with a 400-mapped code: a missing required field, an unknown `op`, or
an operation that refuses a past `asOf`.

`ASOF_INVALID` / `ASOF_IN_FUTURE` — the batch's own `asOf`.

value.message: That request could not be read. Check that the body is valid JSON and that every required value is supplied. (convert-to-native decides from the branch's CURRENT provenance, which a past asOf cannot report; send it without one)

409.description:
An atomic batch failed validation, and the first failure's code was a 409. The body
carries **every** failure in `failures[]`, not just the first — a caller fixing them one
round trip at a time is the behaviour this endpoint exists to avoid.

| code | Cause | Remedy |
|---|---|---|
| `CLAIM_REQUIRED` | a write targeted an inherited row | `claim` it first |
| `ALREADY_CLAIMED` | `claim` on a row this branch already owns | edit it directly |
| `ALREADY_EXCLUDED` | `exclude` on a tombstoned row | `restore` it first |
| `ALREADY_PRESENT` | `add` of a (parent, child) the branch already carries locally; or an op on a **replaced** row | edit the existing row; or act on the substitute |
| `NO_OVERRIDE` | `restore`/`revert`/`convert-to-native` on a row the branch asserts nothing about | nothing to undo |
| `NOT_SUPPLIED` | `revert` on a row no source supplies — falling back would make it vanish | `exclude` instead |
| `STALE_REVISION` | `update` against a revision superseded since your view | reload and retry |
| `NOT_EDITABLE` | the target is inside the subtree of a locally added or substituted assembly | only source-supplied content is editable |

413.description: `BATCH_TOO_LARGE` — more than 200 operations. Split the change.

value.message: A single request can carry at most 200 operations. Split the change into smaller batches. (240 operations, maximum 200)

422.description:
Impossible against the model.

| code | Cause |
|---|---|
| `CYCLE_DETECTED` | the requested edge would make a child an ancestor of its own parent |
| `PARENT_NOT_IN_BRANCH` | `add` targeted a parent that is not part of this configuration |
| `EBOM_CYCLE` | the source eBOM already contains a cycle |
| `UNSUPPORTED_CI_TYPE` | a delta named a CI whose `Type__c` has no registered adapter |
| `CI_IDENTITY_UNRESOLVED` | a CI of a registered type carries no payload row, or one with no join key — corruption, never skipped |
| `CI_IDENTITY_COLLISION` | two `CI__c` rows resolve to one identity, so one of their deltas would be silently discarded |
| `PROVENANCE_INVALID` | a delta named a source that is not this branch's |

value.message: This change would make the child an ancestor of its own parent, which no BOM can represent. (Sub-200 is already an ancestor of Assy-100)

post.summary: Cut a baseline over a branch
post.description:
Records the branch's full effective structure at one timepoint — **as that timepoint**.

## A baseline stores a timepoint, not rows

The cut writes one `Baseline__c` carrying `Resolution_TimePoint__c`, and nothing else about
the content. Reading it back **replays the resolution** at that timestamp, which is exact
because the resolution is a pure function of it and because nothing can ever land at or
before a past T (`Accepted_At__c` and `EffectiveDateTime__c` are both stamped with the wall
clock).

The flattened member table this replaces cost one record per edge per cut — roughly 36 MB at
the measured 18,000-edge ceiling.

## The freeze is what makes the replay honest

A Draft `CI_Rev__c` is edited **in place** by `update`. Replaying a timepoint would therefore
follow an edit made *after* the cut, and the baseline would change without anyone touching
it. So the cut freezes every revision the snapshot resolved to. From then on, every `update`
to those rows forks a new revision instead (and comes back `forked: true`).

## Two timestamps, and why they are not one

`resolutionTimePoint` is what the content was resolved at; `takenAt` is the wall-clock moment
of the cut. Kept apart, a correction to the server clock cannot change what a baseline
resolves to. (MVP-30030 called both `cutDateTime`; the **request** still does, the response
does not.)

## Excluded rows are not members

`memberCount` counts what the configuration *contains*, so tombstoned rows are not counted —
which means it is **not** the number of rows the tree endpoint renders. The baseline read
filters on the same predicate, so the stored count stays comparable to a later read.

## Immutable from the insert

There is no draft-baseline state and no lock step: every update to a `Baseline__c` is refused
outright, and every hard delete too.

## Access

Requires **create** on `Baseline__c`, and **edit** on `Baseline__c` and `CI_Rev__c` (the
freeze). Named separately because a partial grant would otherwise fail half way through the
cut — after the members resolve and before the freeze, the one state a baseline must never
be left in.

backdated.summary: Cut as the configuration stood at an earlier moment

201.description:
The baseline's header. 201 rather than the 200 the delta batch answers: this call names
one new resource, where a batch reports on a set of operations.

400.description:
`INVALID_REQUEST` — unreadable body, or a `label` longer than 80 characters.
`ASOF_IN_FUTURE` — `cutDateTime` is later than now; a baseline of content that does not
exist yet is not a baseline. `ASOF_INVALID` — it could not be parsed.

value.message: A timepoint cannot be in the future. Use now or an earlier moment. (2027-01-01T00:00:00Z)

422.description: `EBOM_CYCLE` — the source eBOM contains a cycle, so nothing can be resolved to cut.

get.summary: Read the rows a baseline captured
get.description:
Re-resolves the branch at the baseline's stored `Resolution_TimePoint__c` and returns the
rows.

## `asOf` is refused, not ignored

Every other tree read on this API takes one, and a client that has been sending it to
`/branches/{id}/tree` will send it here. A baseline **pins its own timepoint**, so a second
one has nothing to answer — accepting it would give the same rows to every value and let a
caller believe they had asked a temporal question and got a temporal answer. Sending `asOf`
is a `400 INVALID_REQUEST`.

`flat` **is** honoured, because that is a shape and not a clock.

## Differences from the branch read

- **Excluded rows are filtered out.** A tree read renders a tombstone so the editor can see
  what was removed; a baseline is the record of what the branch *contained*.
- **`edgeId`, `edgeKey` and the per-row governing clock are suppressed** — a baseline row
  does not pretend to answer questions it cannot. `isReplaced` **is** populated: leaving it
  null would render a substituted part identically to an ordinary one.
- **`warnings` carries drift only.** A `mixed-revision` warning is advice about a branch
  someone is still editing; a baseline is a record of a decision already taken, so it is
  deliberately not forwarded.

## The two drift canaries

| warningCode | What moved |
|---|---|
| `BASELINE_COUNT_DRIFT` | the baseline re-derived a **different number of rows** than its cut recorded — a corrected release date, an edit to an already-released BOM |
| `BASELINE_PROVENANCE_DRIFT` | the same row count, but a **different number of `claimed` rows** — the signature of a `convert-to-native` flipping a row from `claimed` to `local` after the fact |

Both **warn rather than throw**: the rows returned are still the honest answer for the
stored timepoint, and refusing to answer would be worse than answering with a caveat. Two
canaries rather than one because neither can see the other's drift.

200.description: The re-resolved rows. Empty `rows` for a baseline that resolved to nothing is a `200`, not an error.

400.description: `INVALID_REQUEST` — `asOf` was supplied. A baseline is already resolved.

value.message: That request could not be read. Check that the body is valid JSON and that every required value is supplied. (a baseline is already resolved, so asOf has nothing to answer; read the branch if you want a timepoint)

get.summary: Preview the effect of accepting a newer eBOM revision
get.description:
Diffs the eBOM resolved at the source's current T_R against the eBOM resolved at the
candidate root revision's release date, and returns every difference as an individually
addressable entry.

**This call is pure.** It creates and modifies nothing — no `Branch_Member__c`, no
`CI_Rev__c`, no source revision. Calling it twice with the same inputs against an unchanged
org returns identical output, including identical `entryId` values.

**Not every entry is a decision.** Most are informational: the caller is being told what will
happen, not asked. Only `override-orphaned` blocks a commit.

**Already current is not an error.** If the branch already resolves against the newest
released root revision, this returns `200` with `hasChanges: false` and an empty `entries`
array — correct for a read, where a write would throw.

## The correlation key — why a pull doesn't orphan every claim on every release

The two traversals are correlated on **`(Parent_Item__c, Item__c, Secondary_Unique_Key__c)`**
— the legacy `Assembly__c.Tree_Unique__c` with the parent *revision* swapped for the parent
*item*. **Not** on `Assembly_CI__c.Edge_Key__c`.

This is the load-bearing decision of the whole feature. When a parent item revs, Propel
clones its entire BOM into new `Assembly__c` rows with new ids — so a branch that claimed a
line under rev-1 holds a line id that does not exist under rev-2. A join on `Edge_Key__c`
would orphan every claimed edge and re-add every upstream line **on every single pull**. The
parent item does not move when its revision does, which is exactly what lets this key survive
the clone. `Edge_Key__c` still identifies the edge *for display*; it just is not the join key.

`Secondary_Unique_Key__c` rather than `Find_Number__c` because find-number uniqueness is org
configuration, and a key built on it would give two orgs with identical data different diffs.

## The two sides are deliberately asymmetric

- **current** — the branch resolved at the accepted T_R, *with* its own deltas overlaid.
- **candidate** — the **raw** upstream walk at the candidate T_R, with **no overlay at all**.

Overlaying the branch onto the candidate side would match nothing (the deltas are keyed on
line ids that do not exist under the new root) and would append every delta as an unmatched
local edge — which **resurrects the orphans**, correlating a claim on a removed line with the
branch's own edge so `override-orphaned` is never raised. That entry is the only required
decision in the entire feature; silently losing it would make a commit that should block
succeed.

## Entry kinds

| kind | decision | availableActions | Meaning |
|---|---|---|---|
| `source-version-advance` | informational | — | The root item revision advances; nothing structural beneath it changed. |
| `member-version-advance` | informational | — | An edge's child resolves to a newer released revision because T_R moved. |
| `member-added` | informational | — | The candidate adds an edge the branch has no native edge on. Enters automatically. |
| `member-removed` | informational | — | The candidate removes an edge the branch never claimed or replaced. Applies automatically. |
| `override-retained` | informational | — | The branch's override still differs from upstream; the branch wins and upstream is suppressed. `retargeted` distinguishes a suppressed **field value** from a suppressed **re-target**. |
| `override-superseded` | informational | — | The branch's override now *matches* what the candidate would natively produce. |
| `override-orphaned` | **required** | `convert-to-native`, `remove` | The candidate removes an edge the branch **claimed or replaced**. **Blocks the commit.** |
| `member-add-collision` | informational | — | The candidate adds an edge whose correlation key coincides with a branch-**native** edge. The branch's content wins automatically. |

### Why a revision advance is never a decision

A revision is not an independently assertable value. Once you accept that the *line* exists,
which revision it resolves to is a deterministic output of the as-of traversal against T_R —
there is no alternative to offer. The only way to freeze a revision is `claim`, a separate
and heavier operation that takes ownership of the whole edge.

### Why upstream re-pointing an edge at a *different item* is two entries

The correlation key includes the child item, so it never correlates as one matched pair. It
decomposes into an independent `member-removed` (or `override-orphaned`) and an independent
`member-added`. `retargeted: true` therefore means a different child **revision**, not a
different child item.

## Truncation

`entriesLimit` caps how many **informational** entries come back. **`required` entries are
never truncated** — they block the commit, so hiding one would silently conceal a blocker.
`summary` always reports the *untruncated* totals, and `diffFingerprint` always covers the
complete diff, so a truncated response is still safe to commit from.

This call is pure and deterministic, so retrieving more needs no cursor: re-issue with a
larger `entriesLimit` and get back a longer, stable prefix of the same diff.

## Access

**Gated on write, not read.** A read-only user is rejected before a pull is even previewed —
the same `Branch_Source_CI__c` update grant `pull` itself requires.

parameters.name: candidateRootRevisionId
parameters.description:
The released `Item_Revision__c` of the source's root item to preview accepting. When
omitted, defaults to that item's **latest released revision**.

Must belong to the same root item the source already references, must be Released (and
not Cancelled or Expired — the same test that applies when an MBOM is first created), and
must not resolve to a timestamp at or earlier than the source's current T_R.

200.description:
The computed diff, returned bare. Also returned, with `hasChanges: false` and no entries,
when the branch is already current.

changesPending.summary: Assy-100 rev-1 → rev-2, one blocking orphan

alreadyCurrent.summary: Branch already on the newest released revision

truncated.summary: Informational entries capped; the required one survives

400.description:
`INVALID_REQUEST` — `entriesLimit` was not a positive integer. Present-but-unusable is a
400 rather than a silent fallback to the default.

value.message: That request could not be read. Check that the body is valid JSON and that every required value is supplied. (entriesLimit 0)

404.description: `NOT_FOUND` — the source, or `candidateRootRevisionId`, does not exist.

value.message: That record does not exist, or you do not have access to it. (a1Bg8000000AbCdEAK is not a Branch_Source_CI__c)

post.summary: Commit a previewed pull, advancing T_R
post.description:
Accepts a newer eBOM root revision into the branch: appends a new `Branch_Source_CI_Rev__c`
advancing T_R, advances the source's root pointer, and applies the caller's
`override-orphaned` dispositions — **all under one savepoint**.

Returns **`201 Created`**, not 200: a new acceptance record genuinely exists.

## The diff is never trusted from the client

This endpoint **re-resolves the same diff server-side**, through the same code path the
preview used, and answers `STALE_REVISION` the moment the re-resolved `diffFingerprint`
disagrees with what you echoed back, or an `entryId` in `decisions[]` no longer names an
entry in it. Re-preview and resubmit.

A useful side effect: every preview-time failure mode (`NOT_RELEASED`,
`CANDIDATE_ROOT_MISMATCH`, `CANDIDATE_NOT_NEWER`, `CYCLE_DETECTED`, `NOT_FOUND`) applies here
for free — nothing in the commit path re-implements them.

## Decisions

| Situation | Result |
|---|---|
| An `override-orphaned` entry with **no** decision | `409 DISPOSITION_REQUIRED` — the whole commit is rejected. There is no default-accept tier. |
| A decision naming any **other** kind | `400 INVALID_REQUEST` — no other kind is ever actionable. |
| An unrecognised `action` | `400 INVALID_REQUEST`. |

| action | Effect |
|---|---|
| `convert-to-native` | Severs the provenance link, keeping the branch-owned content, which then resolves on the **branch** clock. Runs through the ordinary `convert-to-native` delta operation — every invariant that batch enforces applies unchanged. |
| `remove` | Appends an **exclude** delta (a deletion marker). **Nothing is hard-deleted.** |

## Override reconciliation: reported, never persisted

For every existing claimed/replaced field, the commit compares the override's current value
against what the candidate traversal would natively produce:

- **Differs** → reported as `override-retained` / **reaffirmed**. It stays active and
  continues to govern future pulls. **Nothing new is persisted** — the comparison is
  reconstructed from the accepted source version on every pull, so a "reaffirmation" record
  would change no rendered value.
- **Matches** → reported as `override-superseded`. Also **never deleted and never written**.
  Retiring it would mean a branch that once happened to agree with upstream would silently
  start accepting upstream changes from then on.

`Edge_Key__c` and `Alias__c` are likewise **never re-stamped**. They keep meaning "the
upstream line this edge was originally minted against", independent of the correlation key a
pull actually joins on.

## Atomicity

One outer savepoint around both the disposition batch and the acceptance insert, rolled back
on any exception from either. A failure part way leaves the prior accepted revision and T_R
in place, with no orphaned claim, exclude or override-status records.

## The already-current commit

A commit submitted when the candidate equals the currently-accepted root **still succeeds**:
it appends a new acceptance (advancing `Accepted_At__c` with the same `Source_TimePoint__c`)
and returns `applied: []`. Same reading the preview takes of the read side.

## What a pull leaves alone

Branch-**native** content — anything with no upstream provenance — is entirely unaffected.

## Access

Requires **create** on `Branch_Source_CI_Rev__c`, `Branch_Member__c`, `CI__c`, `CI_Rev__c`,
`Assembly_CI__c` and `Assembly_CI_Rev__c`, **and edit** on `Branch_Source_CI__c`,
`Assembly_CI__c` and `CI_Rev__c`. Both gates run **before the body is read**.

withDisposition.summary: Keep an orphaned claim as branch-owned content

noDecisions.summary: A diff with no required entries

201.description: The pull was committed. A new `Branch_Source_CI_Rev__c` now exists.

400.description:
`INVALID_REQUEST` — the body could not be read; a decision names an entry that is not
`override-orphaned`; or `action` is not one of `convert-to-native` / `remove`.

value.message: That request could not be read. Check that the body is valid JSON and that every required value is supplied. (entryId b7204de9a1c6f358 is member-added, which is never actionable)

404.description: `NOT_FOUND` — the source, or the candidate revision, does not exist.

sessionToken.description:
Standard Salesforce OAuth 2.0 access token or session id, sent as
`Authorization: Bearer <token>`.

BranchId.name: branchId
BranchId.description:
Id of the `Branch__c`. Returned as `branchId` from `POST /mbom/mboms`.

A malformed id, or a well-formed id of the wrong object, is a **404** — not a 500 and not a
403. The URI is what names the resource, so a path naming nothing is a path to nothing, and
the two tree endpoints therefore cannot be confused for each other by a caller that swaps a
branch id for a source id.

SourceId.name: sourceId
SourceId.description:
Id of the `Branch_Source_CI__c`. Returned as **`branchSourceCiId`** from `POST /mbom/mboms`.

In Phase 1 a branch has exactly one source, of `Source_Type__c = 'Ebom'`. The owning branch is
reached through `Branch_Source_CI__c.Downstream_Branch__c`, which is why there is no separate
`branchId` segment on these paths.

BaselineId.name: baselineId
BaselineId.description: Id of the `Baseline__c`, returned from the cut.

AsOf.name: asOf
AsOf.description:
The **branch** clock for this read. Defaults to the server clock when omitted; a future value
is `ASOF_IN_FUTURE` (400).

Governs the branch's own deltas, local content and substitutes. It does **not** govern
inherited content, which always resolves at T_R — that is the two-clock model, and passing
`asOf` to the inherited traversal is the single change that would quietly make a pinned MBOM
float.

Accepts ISO-8601 (`2026-02-01T00:00:00Z`, `2026-02-01T00:00:00+05:30`) and the
space-separated Apex form (`2026-02-01 03:04:05`, interpreted as GMT). A `+` offset is
repaired server-side after query-string decoding turns it into a space, so a legal ISO offset
does not fail in transport.

Flat.name: flat
Flat.description:
Response shape. **Flat is the default, and only an explicit `flat=false` nests.**

Anything unrecognised (`flat=0`, `flat=no`) falls back to flat rather than raising — partly
because `Boolean.valueOf('0')` is `false` and the obvious implementation would *nest* for
`flat=0`, the opposite of what that caller asked for, and partly because a flat response
carries `parentItemId` on every row and is therefore losslessly re-nestable by the client.

Not accepted by `GET /mbom/sources/{sourceId}/tree` — silently ignored there, so one
parameter set can be sent to both tree reads.

EntriesLimit.name: entriesLimit
EntriesLimit.description:
Caps how many **`informational`** entries the preview returns. `required` entries are always
returned in full regardless of this cap.

Must be a positive integer; anything else is `400 INVALID_REQUEST` rather than a silent
fallback to the default.

Provenance.description:
Where a rendered row comes from. **Derived at read time, never stored** — `claimed` and
`local` differ by exactly one field on the winning delta row.

- `inherited` — supplied by the source; no branch-owned record exists.
- `claimed` — the branch took copy-on-write ownership of a source-supplied member.
- `local` — branch-owned with no upstream provenance ("native").

There is no `excluded` value: exclusion is tracked as a separate boolean alongside
provenance, never as a fourth value of it.

GoverningClock.description:
Which clock resolves this member. `source` is the pinned T_R (it only advances when a pull is
committed); `branch` is the caller's `asOf`. Both are legitimately in play at once, which is
what makes mixed revisions of one item possible.

CiType.description:
Discriminator for the configuration-item type, and therefore for the shape of
`MemberState.detail`. `assembly-edge` is the only member type implemented; this enum is the
extension point where a future CI type is added.

`source` appears only on the root-level `source-version-advance` entry's `target` (and on the
root segment of every `path[]`), because that entry is about the source's root **item**
rather than an edge beneath it: it has no parent, no quantity and no find number.

rootItemRevisionId.description:
The **released** `Item_Revision__c` the MBOM is built over. Its `Released_Date_Time__c`
becomes T_R.

mbomName.description:
`MBOM__c.Name`. Required, and a blank value is refused with `INVALID_REQUEST` rather than
being left to DML — a custom object's Text `Name` is unenforced by the API, so a blank
one would silently produce an MBOM named after its own record id that nobody can search
for.

branchLabel.description:
Lands on **both** `Branch__c.Name` (what every Salesforce list view and lookup shows) and
`Branch__c.Label__c`. Bounded by the shorter of the two fields.

branchId.description: The initial `Branch__c`. Use it on every `/branches/...` endpoint.

branchSourceCiId.description:
The `Branch_Source_CI__c` linking the branch to its eBOM. **This is the `sourceId`** on
every `/sources/...` endpoint.

branchSourceCiRevId.description: The first acceptance, carrying T_R in `Source_TimePoint__c`.

MbomTree.description: The response body of **both** tree reads — a branch's effective structure, and a source's structure on its own.

asOf.description: The timepoint this tree was resolved at, echoed so the response is self-describing. Present even when the caller sent none.

rootRevisionId.description: The root `Item_Revision__c` the structure hangs from.

sourceTimePoint.description: **T_R** — the source timepoint inherited rows are pinned at.

rows.description: Always present; empty rather than absent.

warnings.description: Always present; empty rather than absent.

TreeRow.description:
One row of a resolved tree. The same shape serves both response shapes: in the **nested**
shape `childRows` holds the subtree and `parentItemId` is still populated; in the **flat**
shape every row is a sibling and `childRows` is empty — so a client can rebuild the tree from
a flat response without a second request.

edgeId.description: The `Assembly_CI__c` edge. **Null for a purely inherited row** that no branch has claimed. Suppressed on baseline rows.

edgeKey.description:
The legacy `Assembly__c` line id, or a synthetic key for branch-local content:
`local-{branchId}-{parentItemId}-{childItemId}` for an `add`, or
`replaces-{branchId}-{supersededEdgeKey}` for a substitute. Suppressed on baseline rows.

parentItemId.description: The owning **item**, not its revision. Populated in both shapes.

childItemRevisionId.description: The revision this row resolves to at `governingTimestamp`.

governingTimestamp.description: T_R for an inherited row, `asOf` for a local or substituted one. **Null on baseline rows**, where it is suppressed.

sourceId.description: The `Branch_Source_CI__c` this row came from. Null for a branch-local row.

isExcluded.description:
True for a tombstoned row. **Rendered by the branch tree read** so the editor can see
what was removed; **filtered out** by the baseline read.

isReplaced.description: True when this row stands in for another (`replace`). Populated on baseline rows too — a null would render a substituted part identically to an ordinary one.

isEditable.description:
False on any row inside the subtree of a locally added or substituted assembly. Every
delta op refuses those rows, so a UI offering an action on one is offering an action the
API will reject.

findNumber.description: A Salesforce `Number` field, never a string.

childRows.description: Populated in the nested shape only; **empty, never null**, in the flat shape.

TreeWarning.description:
A condition worth telling the user about that does **not** block the read. Shared by the tree
reads, the baseline read and the pull preview.

The key is **`warningCode`**, matching the existing mBOM convention — never `code`, which
this API reserves for the error body.

warningCode.description:
- `MIXED_REVISION` — one item rendered at more than one revision in the same tree,
  because two clocks are in play. Legal and expected; warned, never blocked.
- `BASELINE_COUNT_DRIFT` — a baseline re-derived a different **row count** than its cut
  recorded.
- `BASELINE_PROVENANCE_DRIFT` — a baseline re-derived a different **claimed count**, the
  row count unchanged. The signature of a `convert-to-native` after the fact.
- `NESTED_CYCLE_PRUNED` — the subtree of a locally added assembly was dropped because
  walking it reached a cycle. A warning rather than an error because a local child floats
  at the read clock, so a structure that was acyclic when the `add` was accepted can
  become cyclic when that item is released again — and a read must not fail because
  someone else released an eBOM revision.

message.description: Human-readable, from a Custom Label. Translated; never parse it.

itemId.description: Present on `MIXED_REVISION` — the item rendered at more than one revision.

itemRevisionIds.description: Present on `MIXED_REVISION` — the revisions in play.

governingTimestamps.description: Present on `MIXED_REVISION` — the clock that governed each, positionally aligned with `itemRevisionIds`.

atomic.description:
All-or-nothing when true. **A null is treated as `true`** — the safer contract wins the
default, so a caller who did not think about the failure mode gets all-or-nothing rather
than a half-applied branch.

asOf.description:
Resolves the branch **once** for the whole batch; every operation then validates against
that one snapshot, so a batch cannot see the tree shift underneath it halfway through.

Defaults to the server clock; never accepted in the future. A **past** value means
"validate against the configuration as it stood then" — it never dates the write. Several
operations refuse a past value outright; see the endpoint description.

operations.description: At most 200 — beyond that, `BATCH_TOO_LARGE` (413), refused before anything is resolved.

DeltaOperation.description:
One operation. The shape is a **union across all eight operations** rather than a class per
operation, because the batch arrives as one JSON array. `op` selects which fields are
meaningful, and each operation validates its own required fields — an `add` with no
`parentItemId` is that operation's error to raise, not a deserialisation failure.

Unknown keys are **silently ignored** (the deserialiser is lenient), so a *mistyped* field
name reads as a null id. `rootItemRevisionld` with an `l` will answer `NOT_FOUND`, not a
schema error.

op.description: Matched case-insensitively. An unknown value is a **per-operation** validation failure (`INVALID_REQUEST`), not an exception — one mistyped name in a batch of 200 must not read as a server fault.

clientRef.description:
Opaque caller token, echoed verbatim on this operation's result. Set it to correlate
results with a UI row; the server never interprets it. Correlating on order alone breaks
the moment anything is reordered, and on `clientRef` alone breaks when you do not set it
— so `index` is stated too.

ebomAssemblyId.description: The legacy `Assembly__c` line. Used by: `claim`, `exclude`, `update` (the `CLAIM_REQUIRED` path), `revert` (the second-revert path).

assemblyCiId.description: An existing `Assembly_CI__c` edge to `update`. The ordinary form.

replacedEbomAssemblyId.description: `replace` only — the legacy line being superseded. Must be an eBOM-derived row; a branch-local row cannot be replaced.

newChildItemId.description: `replace` only — the substitute part. Its revision **floats** at the read clock rather than being pinned.

atomic.description: Echoed, so the response says which contract it was written under.

asOf.description:
The timepoint the whole batch resolved against. It matters more here than on a read — the
caller may have sent none at all, and this is the only way to learn which server clock
the batch actually used.

applied.description: Count of operations that succeeded. Stated so a client can act on the summary without walking `results`.

results.description: One entry per requested operation, **in request order**, success or failure.

index.description: Zero-based position of this operation in the request.

clientRef.description: Your own token, echoed verbatim. Null when you set none.

errorCode.description:
An `MbomErrorCode` name on failure, null on success. Note the key is **`errorCode`**
here, inside a per-operation result — the top-level *error body* uses `code`.

message.description: Human-readable, from a Custom Label. Never parsed.

ciId.description: The `CI__c` this operation created or acted on.

assemblyCiId.description: The `Assembly_CI__c` edge this operation created or acted on.

forked.description:
True when an `update` had to allocate a **new** `CI_Rev__c` rather than edit one in
place, because a baseline had frozen it. Surfaced because your next read will show a
revision number you did not ask for.

**Deliberately not defaulted.** Only `update` forks. `null` means *not applicable*
(there was nothing to fork on a `claim` or an `exclude`); `false` means *this write could
have forked and did not*. A client must treat them differently, so the field must be able
to say both.

label.description: `Baseline__c.Name`. Over 80 characters is a 400, not a 500.

cutDateTime.description:
Optional; defaults to the server clock. Becomes `resolutionTimePoint` in the response.
**Never accepted in the future** (`ASOF_IN_FUTURE`) — a baseline of content that does not
exist yet is not a baseline.

The request keeps MVP-30030's caller-facing name; the response returns the two timestamps
that name splits into.

resolutionTimePoint.description: What the baseline resolves against. **Stamped once, never re-derived.**

takenAt.description: The wall-clock moment of the cut. Kept apart from `resolutionTimePoint` so a clock correction cannot change what a baseline resolves to.

memberCount.description:
How many rows the cut resolved, **excluding tombstones**. This is the count of what the
configuration *contains*, not the count of rows the tree endpoint renders. Also the
canary behind `BASELINE_COUNT_DRIFT`.

resolutionTimePoint.description: What the baseline resolved against when it was cut.

rows.description:
The re-resolved rows, reusing the tree shape so clients render both the same way — with
`edgeId`, `edgeKey` and `governingTimestamp` suppressed, and excluded rows filtered out.

warnings.description:
**Drift only** — `BASELINE_COUNT_DRIFT` and `BASELINE_PROVENANCE_DRIFT`. Mixed-revision
warnings from the underlying resolution are deliberately not forwarded: they are advice
about a branch someone is still editing, and a baseline is a record of a decision already
taken.

EntryKind.description:
What kind of change the diff found. Deliberately framed in generic framework terms (source /
member / override) rather than MBOM terms, so the taxonomy survives a second
configuration-item type. See the preview endpoint's table for the full catalog.

Decision.description:
Whether this entry needs the caller to decide anything. **Only two values** — there is no
third, optional-but-defaultable tier. The only decision point anywhere in a pull is disposing
an orphaned override; everything else, including new, removed and colliding upstream content,
applies automatically.

Action.description:
An action the commit endpoint can apply. Both values only ever apply to `override-orphaned`;
a decision naming any other kind is rejected with `INVALID_REQUEST`.

- `convert-to-native` — sever the override's provenance link, keeping its branch-owned
  content, which then resolves on the branch clock. ("Native" is the framework's existing
  term for branch-owned content with no upstream provenance.)
- `remove` — append a deletion marker (an exclude delta). Nothing is hard-deleted.

branchId.description: The owning branch, denormalised for display.

sourceType.description: Only `Ebom` is in scope for Phase 1; `Pull` (branch-to-branch) is reserved.

candidateSourceVersion.description: Absent or null when `hasChanges` is false and no newer revision exists to preview.

hasChanges.description:
False when the branch already resolves against the candidate, or there is no newer
released revision. `entries` is empty in that case. **Not an error condition.**

entries.description:
Every difference found, in a stable, deterministic order. Always present; empty rather
than absent.

warnings.description: Non-blocking conditions — typically `MIXED_REVISION` about what would render *after* the pull. Always present; empty rather than absent.

truncated.description:
True when the **informational** entry set exceeded `entriesLimit` and was trimmed.
Entries with `decision: required` are never truncated. `summary` still reflects the
untrimmed totals.

entriesLimit.description: The effective cap applied this call — the query param, or the server default of 200.

diffFingerprint.description:
Opaque `sha256:`-prefixed digest of the inputs and the **complete** resolved entry set
(not the truncated page). Echo it back on commit; a mismatch means the world moved in
between and fails fast with `STALE_REVISION`.

It covers a **clock-free** projection of the entries, because a claimed row's
`governingTimestamp` *is* the read clock — folding it in would make every commit stale on
arrival.

generatedAt.description: Server clock at computation time. Informational; **not** a resolution input, and not part of the fingerprint.

SourceVersionRef.description:
One version of a source — the accepted eBOM root revision plus the clock that governs
traversal beneath it.

> **Known genericity tension.** `rootItemRevisionId` / `rootItemNumber` / `rootRevisionLabel`
> are PLM-specific: they name an `Item_Revision__c`. Correct for a `Source_Type__c = 'Ebom'`
> source, the only type in Phase 1 scope. When a second source type is implemented, make this
> schema a `oneOf` discriminated on the `sourceType` already present on `PullPreview` — an
> additive change, not a rewrite.

sourceRevisionId.description: The `Branch_Source_CI_Rev__c` recording this acceptance. **Null on `candidateSourceVersion`**, which does not exist until a commit creates it.

resolutionTimestamp.description:
**T_R** — the timestamp the eBOM traversal resolves against. Stamped once at acceptance
from the root revision's release date and read thereafter, never re-derived. Deriving it
per-read would let a later corrected or backdated approval silently rewrite history.

acceptedAt.description: Wall-clock moment the acceptance was committed, kept distinct from `resolutionTimestamp`. Null on `candidateSourceVersion`.

DiffSummary.description: Counts over the **untruncated** entry set, so a caller can render "N informational, M requiring a decision" without walking `entries`.

required.description: Entries that will block a commit until given an explicit decision. Only `override-orphaned` counts here.

byKind.description: Count per `EntryKind`, keyed by kind. Kinds with no entries are omitted.

entryId.description:
Stable, opaque handle, passed back to the commit endpoint to attach a decision. A
**deterministic hash of `kind` plus the correlation key** — never a database Id, never
positional, never generated — so recomputing the same diff yields the same ids. Treat it
as opaque; do not parse it.

availableActions.description: Empty except on `override-orphaned`, whose two dispositions are the only actions this API offers anywhere.

retargeted.description:
**Present only on `override-retained`; `null` on every other kind** (deliberately not
defaulted — a `false` would assert something about a kind for which the question is
meaningless).

True when the suppressed upstream change was a **re-target**: the candidate would resolve
this edge to a different child *revision* than the override pins. False when only field
values (quantity, find number) were suppressed. Lets a caller filter for the
higher-stakes case — a branch silently keeping a superseded revision after upstream moved
on — without parsing `message`.

The child *revision*, not the child *item*: see the endpoint description.

overrideKind.description:
Present on `override-*` kinds; null elsewhere. Distinguishes an override created by
**claiming** an upstream edge from one created by **replacing** it. Both dispose
identically; this exists so the UI can explain what is being orphaned.

message.description: Human-readable, already-localized summary. Never parse it — switch on `kind`.

current.description: How the branch renders this member today. **Null for `member-added`.**

candidate.description: How it would render after the pull. **Null for `member-removed`**, and for an `override-orphaned` resolved by `remove`.

MemberTarget.description: Identifies what the entry is about, independent of before/after state.

edgeId.description: The `Assembly_CI__c` for this member. Null for purely inherited content, which has no branch-owned record until something claims it.

edgeKey.description:
The **display** key — `Assembly_CI__c.Edge_Key__c` / the legacy `Assembly__c` line id.
**Not** what a pull correlates on: it moves when a parent item revs, which is exactly why
the diff cannot join on it.

label.description: Short display label for the member.

path.description: Breadcrumb from the root to this member's parent, for UI context.

PathSegment.description: One ancestor in a breadcrumb. Same shape as `MemberTarget` minus the path — a segment never nests its own breadcrumb.

MemberState.description: A member as resolved at one point in the diff (before or after). The generic fields are framework-level; everything type-specific lives in `detail`.

AssemblyEdgeDetail.description:
**The one MBOM-specific schema.** Everything above this point is reusable framework
vocabulary; this is the single place assembly/BOM concepts appear. A second
configuration-item type becomes a sibling schema in `MemberState.detail`'s `oneOf` and
changes nothing else.

parentItemId.description:
The owning **item**, not its revision. `Assembly_CI__c` carries no parent-revision lookup
at all: a local edge's parent item is stable across revision advances while its parent
revision is not — and `Edge_Key__c` is unique org-wide, so two branches claiming the same
eBOM line share one row, meaning every field on it must be branch-invariant.

childItemRevisionId.description: The child revision this edge resolves to at `governingTimestamp`. Null on a tombstone.

findNumber.description: A Salesforce `Number` field, never a string.

candidateRootRevisionId.description: The released root revision being accepted. Same validation as the preview's query param — and re-validated here, from the re-resolved diff.

diffFingerprint.description: Echoed back from the preview this commit is acting on. A mismatch against the freshly re-resolved diff fails the whole commit with `STALE_REVISION`.

decisions.description:
One entry per `override-orphaned` entry from the preview. **Every one must appear**, or
the commit is rejected with `DISPOSITION_REQUIRED`; naming any other kind is rejected
with `INVALID_REQUEST`. Send `[]` (or omit) when the preview had no required entries.

entryId.description: An `entryId` from the preview this commit is acting on.

newSourceRevisionId.description: The `Branch_Source_CI_Rev__c` this commit created — an **insert**, never an update.

applied.description:
Every entry that took an explicit decision, plus every `override-retained` and
`override-superseded` outcome — the set a caller needs to reconcile its held preview
against what actually happened. (Re-previewing immediately after a commit is always
`hasChanges: false`, so this is the only place to learn it.)

action.description:
The decided action — `convert-to-native` or `remove` — for an `override-orphaned` entry.
Null for a kind that took no decision.

edgeId.description: The branch-owned `Assembly_CI__c` this entry's target names, if any.

RestError.description:
The MBOM's error shape. Keyed **`code`**, not the framework's `errorCode`.

A 403 body carries the label **only**: naming the object a caller was just denied would hand
them the schema they have no access to. It goes to the debug log instead. A 500 *does* carry
the exception type and message — an unmodelled fault has to be diagnosable and its caller is
our own UI or an integration — but never the stack trace.

code.description:
An `MbomErrorCode` name, or `INTERNAL_ERROR` on a 500. `INTERNAL_ERROR` is deliberately
**not** in the enum: every value there is a client error by construction, and a code
exists so a client can branch on it — which it cannot usefully do for a 500.

message.description:
The Custom Label for `code`, with a parenthesised **detail** appended naming the specific
row or value. The label says what went wrong and what to do about it; the detail says
which row it happened to. Translated — never parse it.

failures.description:
Present **only** on an atomic delta batch that failed validation. Carries the complete
per-operation failure list, so a caller does not have to find their faults one round trip
at a time.

Forbidden.description:
`FORBIDDEN` (403). The caller lacks an object grant this endpoint requires. The body names no
object — see `RestError`.

A field-level denial deeper in the stack is also answered 403: under `USER_MODE` that
surfaces as a `QueryException`, and every query on this path is built from a fixed field
list, so an access failure is far and away the likeliest cause.

value.message: You do not have permission to perform this action.

NotFoundPath.description:
`NOT_FOUND` (404). The path id is absent, unparseable, or names a **different object** than
this endpoint expects — the last of which is why swapping a `branchId` for a `sourceId` is a
clean 404 rather than a 500 out of a repository.

Also answered for any unrecognised trailing segment: `GET .../branches/{id}/bogus` is the
MBOM's own 404 in the MBOM's own shape (`code`), not the framework's (`errorCode`).

PullConflictPreview.description:
409 — well formed, retryable after state changes.

| code | Cause |
|---|---|
| `NOT_RELEASED` | the candidate is not Released, or is Cancelled, Expired, or missing a release date |
| `CANDIDATE_NOT_NEWER` | the candidate resolves at or before the source's current T_R |

value.message: That revision is not newer than what this branch already resolves against. Choose a later release, or none is available yet. (a0Ag8000000Ab01EAC)

PullConflictCommit.description:
409 — well formed, retryable after state changes.

| code | Cause | Remedy |
|---|---|---|
| `STALE_REVISION` | `diffFingerprint` mismatch, or an `entryId` that no longer names an entry in the freshly re-resolved diff | re-run `pull-preview` and resubmit |
| `DISPOSITION_REQUIRED` | an `override-orphaned` entry has no decision | supply one for every required entry |
| `NOT_RELEASED` / `CANDIDATE_NOT_NEWER` | revalidated at commit time and no longer qualifies | pick another candidate |

value.message: This row has been revised since the view you are working from. Reload it and try again. (diffFingerprint sha256:9f2c41ab7e08d3b6 no longer matches; re-run pull-preview and resubmit)
This pull orphans an override you made. Choose to keep it as branch-owned content or remove it before committing. (f4880c6b3e1a9d75, ASM-C)

PullUnprocessable.description:
422 — well formed, but impossible against the model. Retrying the identical request will
never succeed.

| code | Cause |
|---|---|
| `CANDIDATE_ROOT_MISMATCH` | the candidate belongs to a **different root item** than the source |
| `CYCLE_DETECTED` / `EBOM_CYCLE` | a cycle in the eBOM below the candidate root |
| `AMBIGUOUS_CORRELATION` | two edges on the **same side** of the diff share a correlation key, so which upstream line matches which branch line cannot be determined — no branch state the caller can reach will fix it |

InternalError.description:
500. Unhandled server-side failure. **Not** an `MbomErrorCode` — the body carries
`INTERNAL_ERROR` plus the exception type and message, and never the stack trace. It is never
answered as a 200: swallowing an unexpected failure would let a half-applied delta batch look
successful.
